clue.text: Quickly capturing hard man in Parisian gang

indicators.note: capturing means the word for quickly holds the letter for hard inside it

parts.note: apace is an old word meaning quickly
H is the pencil-grade abbreviation for hard

explanation.surface: Someone moving fast to catch a tough guy who runs with a Paris street gang.
explanation.walkthrough: An apache was a violent Paris street ruffian of the early twentieth century.
explanation.definitionFit: The Paris underworld of around 1900 called its thugs apaches, after the Native American people.

clue.text: Person who finally runs or coordinates TV programme

explanation.surface: A television producer who also ends up running things.
explanation.walkthrough: The anchorman runs the last leg of a relay race; he also links together a news or current affairs show.
explanation.definitionFit: The final relay runner and the presenter who links a broadcast are both called by this name.

clue.text: High-flier getting a six at the Oval? Right

parts.note: VI is six in Roman numerals
an oval shape is like the letter O

explanation.surface: A star batsman hitting a six at the Oval cricket ground, and quite right too.
explanation.walkthrough: The Oval is a London cricket ground, but here it is just the shape O.
explanation.definitionFit: A pilot flies high in the sky, a literal high-flier.

clue.text: Unpaid workers put up with eccentric views

parts.note: to house a guest is to put them up

indicators.note: eccentric means odd, so the letters of views are arranged oddly

explanation.surface: Volunteers tolerating someone's strange opinions.
explanation.walkthrough: 'eccentric' rearranges VIEWS to WIVES.
explanation.definitionFit: Women running a home do domestic work without wages.

clue.text: Brief captain and sailor to get fish

parts.note: skip is a short, informal form of skipper, a captain
Jack, as in Jack tar, is an old name for a sailor

explanation.surface: A short instruction to the captain and a seaman to go and catch fish.
explanation.definitionFit: The skipjack is a kind of tuna, a sea fish.

clue.text: Book selected by child

parts.note: kid is an informal word for a child
to nap a horse is to select it as the best racing tip

explanation.surface: A novel picked out by a youngster.
explanation.definitionFit: Kidnapped is a novel by Robert Louis Stevenson.

clue.text: Settled home one's in

indicators.note: in means the letter for one goes inside the word for home

parts.note: a pad is slang for a home or flat
I is the Roman numeral one; the 's is read as is

explanation.surface: Someone has moved into their home and settled down.
explanation.definitionFit: A settled bill has been paid off.

clue.text: An old thing in dramatic parts — Mrs Siddons, perhaps

indicators.note: in means the Latin word goes inside the word for parts of a play

parts.note: acts are the main divisions of a play
res is Latin, an old language, for thing

explanation.surface: An antique prop in a play's scenes, used by a famous stage performer.
explanation.walkthrough: Sarah Siddons was the great English tragic actress of the late eighteenth century.
explanation.definitionFit: Sarah Siddons was a celebrated tragedian of the Georgian stage, an example of a female performer.

clue.text: Opener bringing in runs repeatedly for the county

indicators.note: bringing in means the opener's word takes the other letters inside it

parts.note: a key is something that opens a lock

indicators.note: repeatedly says the letter for runs appears twice

parts.note: R is the cricket abbreviation for runs

explanation.surface: An opening batsman piling up runs again and again for his county side.
explanation.walkthrough: The cricket surface hides an Irish county, Kerry.
explanation.definitionFit: Kerry is a county in the south-west of Ireland.

clue.text: Fair, for example — or white, say

explanation.surface: A complexion might be fair or white.
explanation.walkthrough: Fair Isle is a Scottish island; 'white, say' points to the Isle of Wight, whose name is spoken like white.
explanation.definitionFit: Fair Isle is an island in the Shetlands, and Wight is an island off southern England.

clue.text: Sets parts of crosswords without a measure of intelligence

indicators.note: without is used in its old sense of outside, so the word for crossword parts goes round the other piece

parts.note: the clues are parts of every crossword
IQ, intelligence quotient, measures intelligence

explanation.surface: Setting crossword clues that need no brains at all.
explanation.walkthrough: 'without' looks like 'lacking' but is used in its old sense of 'outside'.
explanation.definitionFit: Sets and cliques are both closed groups of people who keep to themselves.

clue.text: One powerless to move monarch following trend

indicators.note: following means the monarch's letters come after those for trend

parts.note: a drift is a general trend or tendency
ER, Elizabeth Regina, is the crossword monarch

explanation.surface: A king or queen whose people are going a certain way, but who cannot do anything about it.
explanation.definitionFit: A drifter moves only as currents carry it, with no power of its own to steer.

clue.text: Do better in theatre, unconscious with anaesthetic

parts.note: someone knocked out cold is out
a general is short for a general anaesthetic

explanation.surface: An operating theatre where the patient is put under with anaesthetic.
explanation.walkthrough: 'theatre' suggests a hospital but is the theatre of war, where generals compete.
explanation.definitionFit: To outmanoeuvre an opponent through superior military leadership in a theatre of war.

clue.text: The company call for a drink

explanation.surface: A firm deciding to order a round of drinks.
explanation.walkthrough: A bevy is a group (of larks or quails, or people); bevy or bevvy is slang for a drink.
explanation.definitionFit: A bevy is a flock or gathering, and in slang the name used for an alcoholic beverage.

clue.text: Bargain hard when after plant

indicators.note: after puts the letter for hard behind the plant's name

parts.note: pennywort is a small round-leaved plant
H is the pencil-grade abbreviation for hard

explanation.surface: Haggling hard over the price of a plant.
explanation.definitionFit: A good pennyworth is old-fashioned for good value for money, a bargain.

clue.text: Views of left-winger harm team's manager, initially

parts.note: to mar something is to harm or spoil it
a cricket or football team is an eleven, XI, with the 's giving S

indicators.note: initially says only the first letter of manager is used

explanation.surface: A political opponent hurting a sports team's boss.
explanation.definitionFit: Marxism is the body of political and economic beliefs held by a follower of Karl Marx, a socialist.

clue.text: Badly handle pessimism an agent displays

indicators.note: displays says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A gloomy agent bungling a job.
explanation.definitionFit: To mismanage is to run something incompetently.

clue.text: "Army" exercise?

parts.note: army read as arm-y, an exercise that works the arms, not a soldiers' drill

explanation.surface: A drill carried out by soldiers.
explanation.walkthrough: The quote marks invite reading 'Army' as 'arm-y': a floor exercise that works the arms.
explanation.definitionFit: Pushing the body up from the floor with the arms is a classic arm-strengthening exercise.

clue.text: Fish with rod — what could be plainer?

parts.note: the pike is a freshwater fish
a staff is a rod or stick

explanation.surface: Going fishing with a rod: nothing could be simpler.
explanation.walkthrough: The idiom 'as plain as a pikestaff' means perfectly obvious.
explanation.definitionFit: The saying 'plain as a pikestaff' makes this pole the byword for obviousness.

clue.text: Book for finishing clues like this one

explanation.surface: A reference work you use to help finish the crossword.
explanation.walkthrough: Every clue, this one included, ends in a figure in brackets giving the letter count; Numbers is also a book of the Old Testament.
explanation.definitionFit: Numbers is the fourth Old Testament book, and figures end every crossword clue as its letter count.

clue.text: Sacred word, quiet restraint for one who trespasses

parts.note: a mantra is a sacred word repeated in meditation
P, piano, is the musical direction for quiet

explanation.surface: A holy word and silence used to keep intruders in check.
explanation.definitionFit: A mantrap is a spring trap once set to catch poachers on private land.

clue.text: Retreat with money from one part of Europe or another

parts.note: a den is a private retreat or study
the mark was the money of Germany, another part of Europe

explanation.surface: Hiding away with cash taken from one European country or another.
explanation.walkthrough: 'from ... or another' says the mark is money of another European country (Germany or Finland), not the one defined.
explanation.definitionFit: Denmark is a Scandinavian country in northern Europe.

clue.text: A superior's assistant

parts.note: better means superior; the 's is read as is

explanation.surface: Someone higher up has a helper.
explanation.definitionFit: An abetter assists or encourages another, usually in wrongdoing.

clue.text: What one has to pay for brandy

explanation.surface: The price someone must pay to get a glass of cognac.
explanation.walkthrough: Fine is a penalty payment; it is also a French brandy (fine champagne).
explanation.definitionFit: A fine is a monetary penalty, and fine is also a good-quality French cognac.

clue.text: Game in which MCC makes 240

explanation.surface: A cricket match in which the MCC scores 240 runs.
explanation.walkthrough: MCC, Roman 1200, is 240 lots of five; fives is also a handball game. The MCC is the Marylebone Cricket Club.
explanation.definitionFit: Fives is a court game played with the hand, and counted in fives, 1200 makes 240.

clue.text: Bigotry confined to head

parts.note: narrow means confined or restricted
a ness is a headland, as in Loch Ness's neighbours or Dungeness

explanation.surface: Prejudice that is all in the mind.
explanation.definitionFit: Narrow-mindedness, a refusal to accept other views, is intolerance.

clue.text: Like anniversary of old Dutch girl

explanation.surface: A wedding anniversary for an old Dutch girl.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Old Dutch' is Cockney slang for one's wife; a fortieth wedding anniversary is a ruby one. Ruby is also a girl's name.
explanation.definitionFit: The fortieth wedding anniversary is named after a red gemstone, which is also a female first name.

clue.text: Dope found within ministry

parts.note: within means in
FO is the Foreign Office, a government ministry

explanation.surface: Drugs discovered inside a government department.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Dope' looks like drugs but is slang for information.
explanation.definitionFit: Dope is slang for information or inside knowledge.

clue.text: Queen seen in museum or gallery

indicators.note: seen in places the letters for Queen inside those for the museum

parts.note: the V and A is the Victoria and Albert Museum in London
ER, Elizabeth Regina, is the queen's cipher

explanation.surface: A queen being spotted in a London museum or art gallery.
explanation.walkthrough: 'gallery' looks like an art gallery but is a veranda, a roofed open gallery along a house.
explanation.definitionFit: A veranda is a roofed platform running along the outside of a house, a kind of open gallery.

clue.text: A bitter exchange, it appears, over a head of the church

definitions.text: over a head of the church

indicators.note: exchange says the letters of these words swap places to form something new

explanation.surface: An angry row breaking out above a bishop.
explanation.definitionFit: A biretta is the square cap worn on the head by Roman Catholic clergy.

clue.text: Speculator has a little drink with model

parts.note: a sup is a small mouthful of drink
a poser is someone who poses, as an artist's model does

explanation.surface: A gambler on the markets having a quick drink with a fashion model.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who supposes is guessing or theorising, so a speculator.

clue.text: Western lawman tailed Arabian governor

indicators.note: tailed means the word loses its tail, its final letter

parts.note: a sheriff is the lawman of every cowboy Western

explanation.surface: A cowboy-film sheriff following an Arab ruler.
explanation.walkthrough: 'tailed' looks like 'followed' but means docked of its tail.
explanation.definitionFit: A sherif (sharif) is a title of an Arab ruler or noble descended from Muhammad.
